items.question: What practice must accompany worship of this circle to produce its effects?
items.inference: Sustained meditation during worship of this circle activates its power.
items.plain_english: Having worshipped this circle, one applies meditation for as long as the practice continues.

items.question: What kinds of languages become perceptible through this meditative practice?
items.inference: The practice grants access to diverse languages, both familiar and previously unknown.
uncertainties: Agreement of aśrutāni/śrutāni with bhāṣās is syntactically loose
items.plain_english: Indeed, languages of various forms, both unheard and heard, arise.

items.question: How are these languages experienced within the practitioner during meditation?
premises: The self is both speaker and hearer
The experience is located within oneself
items.inference: The languages are heard internally, with the self as agent, recipient, and locus.
items.plain_english: They are heard by oneself alone, by oneself to oneself, and within oneself by oneself.

items.question: What bodily transformation results from the successful practice described above?
premises: The practitioner becomes free of wrinkles and grey hair
The resemblance is as a second Kāma
items.inference: The practice confers youthful beauty comparable to a second god of love.
items.plain_english: Freed from wrinkles and grey hair, he becomes like a second Kāma, the god of love.

rows.grounds: object/source to be destroyed; compound vāyu+ādi

items.question: What effect on speech can be produced by destroying the wind and related forces?
premises: The wind and related forces can be destroyed by speech-power
The subject remains like a mute
items.inference: By neutralizing wind-related forces through mantra, one can render a person mute.
uncertainties: Exact referent of vāyvādeḥ (enemy’s breath/speech forces) is context-dependent
items.plain_english: One should destroy the wind and such forces by speech; then he stands like a mute.

items.question: What is the distinctive power attributed to the seventh circle?
premises: It is addressed to the goddess
It is said to paralyze armies
items.inference: The seventh circle possesses the supreme power to immobilize armies.
items.plain_english: O Goddess, the seventh circle is supreme and causes the paralysis of armies.

items.question: From what distance does the seventh circle exert its influence on observers?
premises: The effect relates to that circle
The practitioner is devoted to worship and meditation
items.inference: Even a distant sight of one devoted to this circle’s worship and meditation carries its power.
uncertainties: Whether darśanaṃ means seeing the practitioner or the vision granted is ambiguous
items.plain_english: Indeed, for one devoted to its worship and meditation, its vision has effect even from afar.

items.question: What range of magical operations becomes possible through this seventh circle?
items.inference: The circle enables lethal, expulsive, paralyzing, deluding, and related operations.
items.plain_english: O fortunate one, O beloved, killing, uprooting, paralyzing, deluding, and such acts become possible.

items.question: What knowledge is required for success in the prescribed ritual operations?
premises: The eight-times-eight method must be known
items.inference: Mastery of the eight-times-eight method is a necessary condition for success.
items.plain_english: Indeed, having known the method of the eight groups of eight, one succeeds; not otherwise.

items.question: How should the teaching just declared be received and ascertained by the listener?
premises: The teaching is declared without doubt
It is spoken by the speaker
items.inference: The listener should ascertain this doubtless teaching through both devotion and reasoning.
items.plain_english: Indeed, this has been declared by me without doubt; ascertain it with devotion and reasoning.

items.question: Which chapter concludes in the text that emerged from Candradvīpa?
premises: The text is identified as emerged from Candradvīpa
items.inference: This marks the conclusion of the eighth chapter in the Candradvīpa recension.
items.plain_english: In the text emerged from Candradvīpa, this is the eighth chapter.

items.question: What new topic does the speaker promise to explain to the beloved?
premises: The topic is the arrangement of yoginī rows
It is addressed to the beloved
items.inference: The speaker will now explain the arrangement of the rows of yoginīs.
items.plain_english: O beloved, I shall tell you the arrangement of the rows of yoginīs.

items.question: Which classes of yoginīs are encompassed within the total field being described?
items.inference: The described domain comprises the entire field of earth-moving and sky-moving yoginīs.
uncertainties: gocara interpreted as sky-moving by context; could mean range-moving
items.plain_english: This is the complete field of all earth-moving and all sky-moving yoginīs.

items.question: What additional categories of yoginīs belong to the arrangement being taught?
items.inference: The arrangement includes innate, family-born, and door-guardian yoginīs in their entirety.
items.plain_english: All the innate ones, all those born of the families, and all the door-guardians are included.

items.question: Why has this most secret teaching been revealed to the listener?
premises: The teaching is the supreme secret among secrets
Revelation is granted because of that devotion
items.inference: The supreme secret is revealed to the listener on account of devotion.
items.plain_english: Because of your devotion, the supreme secret of secrets has been revealed.

rows.grounds: object desired to hear; compound siddha+pūjana

items.question: What instruction does the listener now request from the gurus?
premises: The listener expresses a present wish
The wish is to hear from the gurus
The topic is the worship of the siddhas
items.inference: The listener now seeks instruction from the gurus on the worship of the siddhas.
items.plain_english: Now I wish to hear from the gurus about the worship of the siddhas.

items.question: To whom should the arrangement of the two syllables be imparted?
premises: The recipients are among others/outsiders in that context
items.inference: The two-syllable arrangement may be imparted to others as prescribed.
uncertainties: Meaning of anyanteṣu is unclear without wider context
items.plain_english: One should impart the arrangement of the two syllables to others.

items.question: How does this knowledge compare with any knowledge that may arise in the future?
premises: This knowledge is taken as the standard
No equal knowledge will arise again
items.inference: There is and will be no knowledge equal to this one.
items.plain_english: There is no knowledge equal to this, nor will there ever be again.

items.question: What does the speaker promise to explain next to the beautiful-eyed listener?
premises: The speaker addresses the listener directly
A method concerning their names is promised
The listener is asked to hear
items.inference: The speaker will now explain the method of their names.
uncertainties: Referent of teṣāṃ depends on preceding context
items.plain_english: O beautiful-eyed one, listen; I shall speak the method of their names.

items.question: How are the independent impellers of the lineage designated across the four ages?
premises: The group is called family impellers
items.inference: The independent impellers of the lineage are designated as pertaining to the four ages.
uncertainties: Syntactic role of caturyuga as a title is somewhat compressed
items.plain_english: O Lord of Gods, they are called Caturyuga, the independent impellers of the lineage.

rows.grounds: describes extent of kaulaṃ; compound daśa+koṭi+pramāṇa

items.question: What is the extent and origin attributed to this Kaula teaching?
premises: The teaching is identified as Kaula
items.inference: This Kaula teaching is vast in extent and of supreme origin.
uncertainties: daśakoṭipramāṇaṃ may refer to verses, mantras, or beings
items.plain_english: Indeed, this Kaula teaching, supremely arisen, is ten crores in measure.

items.question: By what power and agency does the yoginī named Will operate up to the limit of māyā?
premises: A yoginī named Will is identified
Operation extends up to māyā by supreme will
items.inference: The yoginī Icchā, through the siddhas and by supreme will, operates up to the realm of māyā.
uncertainties: Syntactic relation between siddhaiḥ and māyāntaṃ is compressed
items.plain_english: The yoginī named Icchā, with the siddhas, extends up to māyā by the supreme will.

items.question: Who transmitted the teaching concerning the Mothers in this lineage account?
items.inference: The teaching concerning the Mothers was transmitted by the sky-movers.
items.plain_english: O Goddess, O beloved, it was told again concerning the Mothers by the sky-movers.

rows.grounds: genitive, recipients or subject matter; compound bhū+carī

items.question: Who conveyed the teaching to the auspicious earth-moving yoginīs?
premises: They are described as good eaters
items.inference: The teaching was conveyed to the auspicious earth-moving yoginīs by an earth-mover.
uncertainties: subhakṣāṇāṃ may have a technical tantric sense beyond literal eating
items.plain_english: O beloved, it was told to the auspicious earth-moving yoginīs by an earth-mover.
